content_preview.title: GitHub Copilot CLI and App Add Computer Use in Public Preview, Letting the Agent Operate macOS and Windows Desktop Apps
content_preview.summary: GitHub put computer use into public preview in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app on macOS and Windows; it is off by default and asks approval before controlling an app.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub announced on October 1, 2026 that computer use is [now available in public preview](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-01-github-copilot-can-now-interact-with-desktop-apps) in GitHub Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app on macOS and Windows. The feature lets Copilot operate desktop applications on a user's behalf, extending the coding agent beyond terminals, editors and APIs.

editor_notes.content_quality: Briefing of ~552 words (range 300-800) with Overview, What We Know, Stated Limitations and Risks, What We Don't Know, and Context. Clear, structured, appropriately scoped to two first-party sources.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both snapshots from disk via gunzip (confirmed submission file is the Copilot computer use submission from PR #2523 by title). source-0.html.gz (github.blog changelog, HTTP 200, dated 'October 1, 2026'): confirms 'Computer use is now available in public preview in GitHub Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app on macOS and Windows'; capability list (reading accessible app content and visual context, clicking controls, entering and editing text, pressing keys, scrolling, dragging, navigating workflows); legacy/GUI-only software without API, CLI or MCP integration; 'Copilot asks for approval before controlling an app, and you can review or reset apps that you have chosen to always allow'; macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording guidance; 'Organization-managed settings can disable the feature'; /computer on, /computer show, /computer off; app path Settings > Computer Use > Enable Computer Use; examples (summarize notifications in a browser, update content in a presentation). source-1.html.gz (docs.github.com 'About computer use in GitHub Copilot', HTTP 200, raw 469 KB HTML, full docs text, not a summary): confirms 'Computer use is in public preview and subject to change.'; 'available in GitHub Copilot CLI and GitHub Copilot app on macOS and Windows'; 'Computer use is disabled by default. You must enable it before an agent can use its tools.'; accessibility tree or screenshots; Always allow stored locally and applies to both CLI and app; enterprise administrators can disable via managed settings and 'Enabling computer use locally does not override an enterprise policy'; Esc twice in CLI, Stop or Esc in app; the wrong-control/wrong-location limitation; the Warning callout, quoted verbatim in the article: 'Computer use can automate interactions across desktop applications, but it also introduces security risks.' (the article's further paraphrase of the Warning and the Always allow advice and the Tip about API/MCP/terminal tools all match the page). The security warning is correctly attributed to GitHub's documentation, not writer analysis. Extra-scrutiny points: (1) public preview, macOS and Windows, CLI and app, Oct 1 verified; Linux is not mentioned in either source, and the article correctly places it under 'What We Don't Know' rather than asserting it is unsupported. (2) off by default, approval prompts, and the warning verified verbatim. (3) Neither source names Copilot plans/eligibility; the article makes no plan claim and only reports the admin/enterprise policy control, which both sources state. (4) The docs snapshot is the full raw docs page containing the cited Warning, Tip and Limitations text. (5) No speculation about internals; the only mechanism described (accessibility tree or screenshots) is the docs' own wording. (6) Both cross-references resolve to existing files: 2026-09/25-github-copilot-app-adds-local-sandboxing-off-by-default-to-contain-unintended-agent-commands.md and 2026-03/24-anthropic-brings-computer-use-to-macos-as-claude-gains-ability-to-control-desktop-apps-autonomously.md; context claims (sandboxing off by default; Anthropic research preview for Mac) match those articles. Domains: github.blog and docs.github.com are both on config/source_allowlist.txt. suspicious_patterns: null for both sources, nothing to evaluate. Both URLs in article.sources match the body URLs (no orphans). No outside coverage is cited; the article is entirely first-party and attributes claims accordingly.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific (date, platforms, surfaces, commands, settings path, permissions, key combos, quoted warning) traces to the snapshots. No fabrication found. Minor framing: 'extending the coding agent beyond terminals, editors and APIs' in the lead is a light paraphrase of the sources' 'legacy and GUI-only software' language; not a factual issue.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributed throughout; risks reported as GitHub's own statements.
editor_notes.originality: No existing article covers Copilot computer use. Related prior articles (Copilot app local sandboxing, 2026-09-25; Anthropic computer use on macOS, 2026-03-24) are different stories, referenced as context only.
concerns: Neither source states plan/eligibility or Linux support; article appropriately does not claim either.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced first-party briefing with verbatim-correct warning attribution. Approved for publication without corrections.
